## Proof

**Setup.** Label rows and columns $1$ through $8$. Give the board its standard chess coloring, so adjacent squares have opposite colors; a square $(i,j)$ is white iff $i+j$ has a fixed parity (the choice of parity will not matter). A horizontal domino with left square $(i,j)$ (covering $(i,j)$ and $(i,j+1)$) is type $L$ exactly when the left square is white. Thus, up to an overall sign,

$$N_L - N_R = \sum_{\text{horizontal dominoes}} (-1)^{i+j},$$

where $(i,j)$ is the left square of the domino. We will show this sum is always $0$.

**Key invariant.** For each column $j\in\{1,\dots,8\}$, consider the alternating row sum

$$C_j = \sum_{i=1}^{8} (-1)^i,$$

computed over the eight squares in column $j$. Since there are four odd and four even rows, $C_j = 0$ for every $j$.

Now account for $C_j$ domino-by-domino. Each square $(i,j)$ is covered by exactly one domino:

- If it is covered by a **vertical** domino in column $j$, that domino also covers $(i\pm 1, j)$, contributing $(-1)^i + (-1)^{i\pm 1} = 0$ to $C_j$.
- If it is covered by a **horizontal** domino, that domino has left column $j-1$ or $j$, and the square $(i,j)$ contributes $(-1)^i$ to $C_j$.

Let $h_k = \sum_{\text{horizontal dominoes with left column } k} (-1)^{\text{row}}$, for $k=1,\dots,7$. A horizontal domino with left column $k$ touches columns $k$ and $k+1$, so

$$C_j = \begin{cases} h_1 & j=1,\\ h_{j-1}+h_j & 2\le j\le 7,\\ h_7 & j=8. \end{cases}$$

Since every $C_j=0$:

- $C_1 = h_1 = 0$.
- $C_2 = h_1 + h_2 = 0 \Rightarrow h_2 = 0$.
- $C_3 = h_2 + h_3 = 0 \Rightarrow h_3 = 0$.
- $\;\vdots$
- $C_7 = h_6 + h_7 = 0 \Rightarrow h_7 = 0$ (and $C_8 = h_7 = 0$ is consistent).

By induction, $h_k = 0$ for every $k=1,\dots,7$.

**Conclusion.** Grouping the horizontal dominoes by their left column,

$$N_L - N_R = \sum_{k=1}^{7} (-1)^{k}\, h_k = \sum_{k=1}^{7} (-1)^k \cdot 0 = 0.$$

This holds for **every** domino tiling of the $8\times 8$ board, regardless of the white/black parity convention (flipping the convention only negates the sum, which is already $0$). Hence $N_L = N_R$ always, and

$$\max\, |N_L - N_R| = 0.$$

## Proof

**Setup.** Label rows and columns $1$ through $8$. Give the board its standard chess coloring, so adjacent squares have opposite colors; a square $(i,j)$ is white iff $i+j$ has a fixed parity (the choice of parity will not matter). A horizontal domino with left square $(i,j)$ (covering $(i,j)$ and $(i,j+1)$) is type $L$ exactly when the left square is white. Thus, up to an overall sign,

$$N_L - N_R = \sum_{\text{horizontal dominoes}} (-1)^{i+j},$$

where $(i,j)$ is the left square of the domino. We will show this sum is always $0$.

**Key invariant.** For each column $j\in\{1,\dots,8\}$, consider the alternating row sum

$$C_j = \sum_{i=1}^{8} (-1)^i,$$

computed over the eight squares in column $j$. Since there are four odd and four even rows, $C_j = 0$ for every $j$.

Now account for $C_j$ domino-by-domino. Each square $(i,j)$ is covered by exactly one domino:

- If it is covered by a **vertical** domino in column $j$, that domino also covers $(i\pm 1, j)$, contributing $(-1)^i + (-1)^{i\pm 1} = 0$ to $C_j$.
- If it is covered by a **horizontal** domino, that domino has left column $j-1$ or $j$, and the square $(i,j)$ contributes $(-1)^i$ to $C_j$.

Let $h_k = \sum_{\text{horizontal dominoes with left column } k} (-1)^{\text{row}}$, for $k=1,\dots,7$. A horizontal domino with left column $k$ touches columns $k$ and $k+1$, so

$$C_j = \begin{cases} h_1 & j=1,\\ h_{j-1}+h_j & 2\le j\le 7,\\ h_7 & j=8. \end{cases}$$

Since every $C_j=0$:

- $C_1 = h_1 = 0$.
- $C_2 = h_1 + h_2 = 0 \Rightarrow h_2 = 0$.
- $C_3 = h_2 + h_3 = 0 \Rightarrow h_3 = 0$.
- $\;\vdots$
- $C_7 = h_6 + h_7 = 0 \Rightarrow h_7 = 0$ (and $C_8 = h_7 = 0$ is consistent).

By induction, $h_k = 0$ for every $k=1,\dots,7$.

**Conclusion.** Grouping the horizontal dominoes by their left column,

$$N_L - N_R = \sum_{k=1}^{7} (-1)^{k}\, h_k = \sum_{k=1}^{7} (-1)^k \cdot 0 = 0.$$

This holds for **every** domino tiling of the $8\times 8$ board, regardless of the white/black parity convention (flipping the convention only negates the sum, which is already $0$). Hence $N_L = N_R$ always, and

$$\max\, |N_L - N_R| = 0.$$
